U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs, (1974) provides the following generalities from the above data: 
   With one exception, all analyses indicate that the water is extremely high in hardness; the lowest hardness is from a well in the Lebo shale-Tullock member aquifer.
   Varied water quality is found in the alluvium along the major water courses.
3. Water quality in the Rosebud-McKay overburden and coal seam aquifers is characterized by high calcium and magnesium concentrations in the forms of calcium sulfate and magnesium sulfate.
4. High sodium as sodium sulfate and sodium bicarbonate is present in water from the Robinson coal seam aquifer.
5. Water in the Lebo shale-Tullock member aquifer is high in sodium sulfate and sodium bicarbonate. The sodium-adsorption-ratio of this water is generally excessivly high.
6. Lowest dissolved solids occur in the Rosebud-McKay aquifer; the highest occur in the alluvium and Lebo-Tullock aquifers.
7. Iron is found in the ground water, probably as iron sulfate.
8. Specific quality of ground water in many of the deeper aquifers on Tract III is unknown. It is probable that the Parkman
sandstone and Cloverly formation contain slightly brackish
water, characterized by predominant concentrations of sodium
bicarbonate and sodium sulfate. The high salinity and sodium\nprecludes the use of this water for agricultural purposes.
